title: create.sh --track <track>/<sub-track> writes through a symlinked sub-track that every reader skips
scopeProof: --track is user input accepted by validate_track_value; the two-segment form is the new sub-track form this packet introduces.
claim: create.sh follows a symlinked sub-track and scaffolds a packet through it even though track-roots treats that folder as skipped and never refreshes it.

title: A linked description.json declares a sub-track in validation and archive but not in track-roots or the repair path
scopeProof: All five implementations read the same declaration field from the same folder; the disagreement is reachable by replacing a real description.json with a symlink.
claim: The tools disagree on whether a symlinked description.json declares a sub-track, producing an exempted validator/archiver container that the track readers do not see.

title: A three-segment --track value scaffolds a packet at a depth no reader scans
scopeProof: --track is caller input; the three-segment value passes every refusal in validate_track_value.
claim: A three-segment --track passes validate_track_value and creates a packet that no track reader or recursive validation reaches.

title: The doctor host-relative alias check is lexical; a host symlink inside the root can make the mirrored alias resolve outside it
scopeProof: The function's stated purpose is to keep a host-sibling alias inside the host; the target check is the only gate before op:link.
claim: The host-target containment check uses a lexical path comparison while the target is later resolved through the host filesystem, so a host symlink can move the alias outside the root.
